description: The .event class used in the Aktuelles (Current Events) section wraps individual event articles but has no CSS styling. Events contain important information about upcoming exhibitions.

phases.name: Analysis & Design
phases.description: Analyze existing patterns and design the event card styling approach

subtasks.title: Document existing design patterns
subtasks.description: Record discoveries about the existing CSS design system including variables, spacing patterns, and similar component styles (event-card, exhibitions-list) to ensure new styling follows established conventions.
acceptance_criteria: Document CSS custom properties to use (colors, spacing, typography, shadows, radius)
Identify existing similar patterns (event-card, section-content styles)
Record responsive breakpoints used in the project
subtasks.notes: Documented comprehensive CSS design system including: color variables (primary, accent/tint #FF1493, borders, backgrounds), spacing system (base 1.5rem with xs/sm/md/lg/xl variants), shadows (sm/md/lg), border radius (sm/md/lg), transitions (fast/base), typography (Georgia serif, 5 font sizes), responsive breakpoints (767px, 1024px). Analyzed reference patterns: .event-card (card styling with border, radius, padding), .photo-gallery-item (hover with translateY and shadow upgrade), .exhibitions-list (custom bullets with accent color). Identified .event HTML structure in index.njk with h3 and paragraphs containing strong labels.

phases.name: Implementation
phases.description: Implement CSS styling for the .event class

subtasks.title: Add base .event styles
subtasks.description: Add CSS rules for the .event class with proper card styling including background, border, border-radius, padding, and spacing between events. Use existing design tokens.
acceptance_criteria: Event articles have card-like appearance with background, border, and rounded corners
Proper spacing between multiple event articles
Uses existing CSS custom properties (--color-*, --spacing-*, --radius-*, --shadow-*)
subtasks.notes: Successfully added CSS rules for .event class with card styling. Includes background-color, border, border-radius, padding, margin-bottom for spacing, and box-shadow. All styling uses existing design tokens (--color-background, --color-border, --radius-md, --spacing-md, --shadow-sm). Follows established patterns from .event-card class. Changes committed to git.

subtasks.title: Add .event heading styles
subtasks.description: Style the h3 headings within .event articles to create clear visual hierarchy. The heading contains the event date and title.
acceptance_criteria: Event headings have appropriate font size and weight
Optional accent color to highlight dates/titles
Proper margin below heading
subtasks.notes: Successfully added CSS styling for .event h3 headings. Includes font-size: var(--font-size-medium), font-weight: var(--font-weight-bold), appropriate line-height: var(--line-height-heading), and margin-bottom: var(--spacing-sm) for proper spacing. Uses existing design tokens throughout. Creates clear visual hierarchy for event dates and titles. Changes committed to git.

subtasks.title: Add .event paragraph styles
subtasks.description: Style paragraphs within .event articles containing location, time, and date information. Ensure labels (Ort, Vernissage, Zeit) are visually distinct.
acceptance_criteria: Paragraphs have appropriate line-height and spacing
Strong elements (labels) are visually distinct
Last paragraph has no bottom margin
subtasks.notes: Successfully added CSS styling for .event paragraphs and strong elements. Paragraphs include line-height: var(--line-height-base) and margin-bottom: var(--spacing-sm) for proper spacing. Strong elements (labels like Ort, Vernissage, Zeit) styled with font-weight: var(--font-weight-bold) and color: var(--color-accent) for visual distinction. Last paragraph has margin-bottom: 0 to prevent extra spacing. All styling uses existing design tokens. Changes committed to git.

subtasks.title: Add hover/focus states
subtasks.description: Add subtle interactive states to event cards for better UX, following patterns from photo-gallery-item hover states.
acceptance_criteria: Subtle hover effect (shadow or transform)
Smooth transition using existing transition variables
subtasks.notes: Successfully added subtle interactive states to event cards. Includes transition property for smooth animations (transform and box-shadow using --transition-fast), hover and focus-within states with translateY(-4px) lift effect, and shadow upgrade from --shadow-sm to --shadow-md. Implementation follows the exact pattern from .photo-gallery-item hover states. All styling uses existing design tokens. Changes committed to git (commit 7c47e1f).

subtasks.title: Add responsive styles
subtasks.description: Add media queries to adjust event card styling for mobile and tablet breakpoints following existing patterns (767px, 1024px).
acceptance_criteria: Event cards look good on mobile (< 768px)
Appropriate padding/spacing adjustments for smaller screens
subtasks.notes: Successfully added responsive media queries for .event cards following established breakpoint patterns (767px, 1024px). Mobile styles (max-width: 767px) reduce padding and margin-bottom from var(--spacing-md) to var(--spacing-sm), and reduce h3 font-size from var(--font-size-medium) to var(--font-size-base) for better mobile readability. Desktop styles (min-width: 1024px) increase padding from var(--spacing-md) to var(--spacing-lg) for enhanced spacing on larger screens. All styling uses existing design tokens. Changes committed to git (commit 67ef673).

phases.name: Testing & Verification
phases.description: Test the implementation and verify it works correctly

subtasks.title: Build and visual verification
subtasks.description: Run the Eleventy build process to verify no errors and check that styles are applied correctly.
acceptance_criteria: npm run build completes successfully
CSS file is generated without errors
Event articles are visually styled in the built output

subtasks.title: Cross-browser and responsive testing
subtasks.description: Verify styles work across the responsive breakpoints by inspecting the generated CSS.
acceptance_criteria: CSS contains proper media queries
Styles follow mobile-first or desktop-first approach consistently with existing code

final_acceptance: Event articles in Aktuelles section are visually styled as cards
Event information (date, location, time) is scannable and well-organized
Styling follows existing design system patterns
Responsive design works on mobile and desktop
